Mali.title: Tinzaouatène, Kidal, Niono and Sofara: The FAMa intensify strikes against armed terrorist groups
Mali.summary: Supported by their partners, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) targeted both the logistical and financial networks and the armed terrorist groups involved in recent attacks, neutralising several dozen fighters and destroying significant material resources.

Mali.title: Au Mali, les morts discrets de l’Africa Corps
Mali.summary: RÉCIT - Le Guardian révèle qu’au moins 349 soldats russes sont morts au cours des trois dernières années en appuyant la junte au pouvoir à Bamako. Passer la publicitéDans l’océan des pertes militaires russes, les morts tombés au Mali ne sont qu’une goutte d’eau. Près de 350 hommes ont été tués dans le désert sur les quelque 700 000 morts qu’a enregistrés l’armée russe ces dernières années.

Mali.title: Mali : Assimi Goïta réunit les chefs d'état-major et fixe ses priorités militaires
Mali.summary: Au Mali, le général d’armée Assimi Goïta a réuni mardi 24 novembre 2026, au matin, les chefs d’état-major et les responsables de services des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité (FDS). Le chef de l’État, également chef suprême des Armées, voulait faire le point sur la sécurité du territoire et sur la collaboration entre les unités. « La mobilisation et l’efficacité des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité demeurent une priorité absolue », écrit l’état-major dans son communiqué publié le lendemain.

Mali.title: Mali : le Jnim somme les habitants de Tonka de partir, en réaction à la présence de l'armée
Mali: The Transitional President Holds Discussions with the Military Command
Mali.summary: On Tuesday, 24 November 2026, in Koulouba, the President of Mali's Transition and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, General Assimi Goïta, chaired a meeting with the Chiefs of Staff and Directors of Services of the Defence and Security Forces (FDS). . According to the Malian Presidency, the aim of this meeting was to assess the situation of the forces, strengthen the coherence of command, and define the strategic and operational priorities of national defence.

Burkina Faso.title: African Tirailleur Day: A tribute to their memory and a show of solidarity
Burkina Faso.summary: African Tirailleur Day was commemorated on Thursday, 26 November 2026, at Place de la Révolution in Ouagadougou, under the theme 'Veterans' Commitment: What Lessons Can We Learn?'. The ceremony highlighted the continuity of the patriotic struggle, with tributes to veterans, a call for discipline among the forces involved and the presentation of a financial contribution to the national effort.

Burkina Faso.title: Entre Nous: “Exploring the path to dialogue with JNIM”
Burkina Faso.summary: On 20 November 2026, the International Crisis Group published a report entitled: "The Battle for Cities: Countering the JNIM Threat to Sahel Urban Centres". According to this international non-profit NGO, whose mission is to prevent and help resolve deadly conflicts through field research, analysis and political advocacy, "the human cost of the conflict is already considerable and continues to rise".

Burkina Faso.title: Career change: 3,014 VDPs soon to be trained in over 40 professions
Burkina Faso.summary: The Brigade of Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland and the public institution Burkina Suudu Bawdè (BSB) signed a partnership agreement for the training and socio-economic reintegration of 3,014 Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDPs) at the end of their service, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, in Ouagadougou.

Niger.title: Why are jihadist groups kidnapping civilians in the Sahel?
Niger.summary: A Saudi national was reportedly kidnapped by jihadist groups last weekend. According to sources contacted by the Reuters news agency, the kidnapping reportedly took place in Niger, in the Tillabéry region, in the tri-border area. So far, there has been no comment from either country, but the kidnapping of civilians is an important source of funding for jihadist groups.

Niger.title: Insecurity: 11 soldiers killed and 22 attackers neutralised in a Boko Haram attack in Baroua (Diffa)
Niger.summary: In a statement issued on 24 November, the Ministry of Defence announced that eleven (11) Nigerien soldiers had lost their lives and several others had been injured in a terrorist attack attributed to Boko Haram in Baroua, in the Diffa region, in the far south-east of the country. According to the same source, in their response, the defence and security forces neutralised 22 attackers, and pursuit and sweep operations were immediately launched in this border area of Lake Chad.
